title: Bankruptcy automatic stay: what a filing stops and its main limits
rule: A bankruptcy petition stays, as to all entities: starting or continuing a proceeding against the debtor that was or could have been started before the case, or to recover a prepetition claim; enforcing a prepetition judgment; taking possession or control of estate property; creating, perfecting or enforcing a lien against estate property; collecting a prepetition claim; and setting off a prepetition debt owed to the debtor. The stay does not bar a lessor from recovering nonresidential real property under a lease whose stated term expired before or during the case. After notice and a hearing, the court grants relief from the stay for cause, including lack of adequate protection.
changeWatch: Pub. L. 119-27 (July 18, 2025) adds a stablecoin-redemption item to 362(a) and a relief ground as 362(d)(5), effective 18 months after enactment (January 18, 2027) or 120 days after final implementing regulations, whichever is earlier; any other amendment to section 362.

sources.title: 11 U.S.C. 362, Automatic stay (subsection (a))
sources.quote: any act to obtain possession of property of the estate or of property from the estate or to exercise control over property of the estate
